result.target_topic: Q1 2024 Goodwill Impairment for Intel Foundry
result.target_summary: Following a segment reporting modification in Q1 2024, Intel recognized a $222 million goodwill impairment loss for the Intel Foundry reporting unit, resulting in zero remaining goodwill for that unit. The impairment occurred because the fair value of the new reporting unit, which included substantially all allocated property, plant, and equipment, was lower than its carrying value.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Company conducted annual qualitative impairment tests for goodwill in the fourth quarters of fiscal years 2024 and 2023 and concluded that there was no goodwill impairment for its reporting units.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the results of their goodwill impairment testing for fiscal year 2024. Intel recognized a $222 million non-cash impairment loss for its Intel Foundry reporting unit due to a segment reorganization where fair value fell below carrying value. In contrast, AMD conducted qualitative impairment tests for its reporting units in the fourth quarter of 2024 and concluded that no goodwill impairment existed.

sentences.text: As a result of our post-reorganization impairment test, we recognized a non-cash goodwill impairment loss of $222 million within restructuring and other in the first quarter of 2024 related to our Intel Foundry reporting unit, as the estimated fair value of the new reporting unit was lower than the assigned carrying value, which includes substantially all of our allocated property, plant, and equipment.
The Intel Foundry reporting unit has no remaining goodwill.

During the fourth quarter of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, the Company conducted its annual qualitative impairment tests of goodwill and concluded that there was no goodwill impairment with respect to its reporting units.

comparisons.peer_summary: Due to macroeconomic challenges and reduced customer demand in 2023, the company recognized a $101 million goodwill impairment charge for its SBU reporting unit; quantitative assessments for other reporting units showed fair values substantially exceeding carrying values.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies report specific goodwill impairment charges recognized in their fiscal year reports. Intel recognized a $222 million impairment loss in Q1 2024 for the Intel Foundry unit after reallocation. Micron recognized a $101 million charge in 2023 for its SBU reporting unit due to macroeconomic challenges and reduced demand. While the amounts and specific units differ, both disclosures detail significant impairments resulting from fair value assessments falling below carrying values.

sentences.text: As a result of our post-reorganization impairment test, we recognized a non-cash goodwill impairment loss of $222 million within restructuring and other in the first quarter of 2024 related to our Intel Foundry reporting unit, as the estimated fair value of the new reporting unit was lower than the assigned carrying value, which includes substantially all of our allocated property, plant, and equipment.
The Intel Foundry reporting unit has no remaining goodwill.

We recognized a $101 million charge in 2023, included in other operating income (loss) to impair all of the goodwill assigned to our SBU reporting unit based on our best estimates of projected future cash flows at that time.
The 2023 quantitative assessment for all of our other reporting units yielded fair values that substantially exceeded their carrying values.
